f.title: Report extremely harmful side effects recorded during clinical trials to the Authorised Body
f.statement: The Contracting Authority (sponsor) for clinical trials is obliged to inform the Authorised Body, in the manner and within the time limit prescribed by the Authorised Body, of cases of extremely harmful side effects recorded during the trials (fatal, life-threatening, requiring hospitalisation, resulting in incapacity for work, physical mutation, inborn defect), as well as of amendments to the trial documents and the start, termination or end of the trial, and must submit a report in the form prescribed by the Authorised Body.

rows.deadline: Time limit prescribed by the Authorised Body
rows.quote: 10. The Contracting Authority for clinical trials shall be obliged to inform — in the manner and within the time limit prescribed by the Authorised Body — of the amendments made in the documents submitted for clinical trial permit and of cases of extremely harmful side effects recorded during the trials (fatal, posing risk to life, requiring hospitalisation, resulting in incapacity for work, physical mutation, inborn defect), start, termination or end of trials, as well as submit a report in the form prescribed by the Authorised Body.
rows.review_note: Review: kept as one row because the time limits and form are delegated to the Authorised Body (MoH Order 322-N, curated as am-moh-order-322-n-2024, points to EAEU GCP/GVP). ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Pay for GCP monitoring and act on Authorised Body requests to modify or stop the trial
f.statement: The Authorised Body supervises clinical trials and the safety of investigational products through GCP conformity monitoring at trial sites (including contractors). The sponsor compensates the expenses of the professional monitoring under contract, and the Authorised Body may request the sponsor to modify or supplement the trial programme or terminate the trial; the procedure for safety monitoring and termination is set by the Authorised Body.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Audit & inspection readiness

rows.quote: The expenses for professional monitoring shall be compensated by the contracting authority for clinical trials, based on the contracts concluded between the parties as prescribed by law. The expert opinion drawn up based on professional monitoring shall be submitted to the Authorised Body. The Authorised Body shall be competent to request the Contracting Authority to modify the clinical trial programme, make supplements in the programme or terminate the clinical trials.
rows.review_note: Review: quote trimmed to the sentences on expenses and modification or termination requests (part 11 is over 1000 characters); the supervision and procedure sentences are paraphrased from the same part. Authority powers kept because they set the sponsor's duty to pay and to act on modification or termination requests. ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Terminate a clinical trial when participants are at risk or safety is not proven
f.statement: Clinical trials shall be terminated where the health or life of a trial subject is at risk, where the legal, ethical or Good Clinical Practice requirements are violated, or where the effectiveness and safety of the medicine or investigational product are not proven.

rows.actor: Contracting Authority for clinical trials (sponsor) and Authorised Body
rows.quote: 12. Clinical trials shall be terminated where the health and (or) life of a person subject to trial is at risk, the requirements for clinical trials prescribed by this Law, medical ethics norms of requirements for Good Clinical Practice adopted by the Authorised Body are violated, as well as the effectiveness and safety of medicine or researched pharmaceutical product are not proven.
rows.review_note: Review: the law does not name who terminates; sponsor and Authorised Body both recorded. ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Remain responsible for product safety and promptly notify new post-registration data, including foreign bans
f.statement: The MAH is responsible, as prescribed by law, for the safety, efficacy and quality of the registered product and is obliged to promptly notify the Authorised Body in writing of each new data on the product and of modifications identified or made in the post-registration period, including data of the competent body of any country on prohibition or restriction of the product's use.
f.clause: Article 16. State registration of medicines, part 22
f.processes: Reporting policy; Submission operations; Signal management

rows.actor: Holder of the certificate of registration (marketing authorisation holder)
rows.quote: 22. The holder of the certificate of registration of the medicine shall be responsible, as prescribed by law, for the safety, efficacy, quality of the registered product, and shall be obliged to promptly notify the Authorised Body in writing of each new data on the registered product and (or) modification thereof being identified and (or) made in the post-registration period, including the data of the competent body of any country on prohibition or restriction on the use of the product.
rows.location: Article 16. State registration of medicines, part 22
rows.review_note: Review: "promptly" with no number, so no deadline_rule. ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Registration may be revoked if an unfavourable benefit-risk is confirmed or the MAH obstructs monitoring
f.statement: The registration of a medicine shall be revoked where, among other grounds, post-registration professional monitoring confirms an unfavourable risk-benefit ratio, or where the MAH refused to comply with its obligations under the Law, hindered post-registration professional monitoring or failed to correct inconsistencies found during that monitoring.
f.clause: Article 16. State registration of medicines, part 29

rows.actor: Holder of the certificate of registration (marketing authorisation holder)
rows.location: Article 16. State registration of medicines, part 29
rows.review_note: Review: sanction tied to PV duties; quote includes point (5) (manufacturing termination) because points 4-6 run consecutively. ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Registration is suspended if the MAH fails to provide new safety data or update the dossier
f.statement: The registration of a medicine shall be suspended where the MAH failed to provide new data on the quality, safety or efficacy of the product or failed to modify the registration documents in line with the new data; the suspension lasts until the violation is eliminated.
f.clause: Article 16. State registration of medicines, part 31

rows.actor: Holder of the certificate of registration (marketing authorisation holder)
rows.quote: (3) the holder of the certificate of registration failed to provide the new data regarding the quality, safety or efficacy of the product or failed to make modifications to the registration documents in line with the new data;
rows.location: Article 16. State registration of medicines, part 31
rows.review_note: Review: the duration ("until the violations or inconsistencies are eliminated") is in part 32, not in the quote. ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: MAH obligations pass to the importer when the MAH withdraws from Armenia
f.statement: Where the MAH notifies the Authorised Body in writing of its intention to terminate its obligations in Armenia, the medicine remains registered until the registration term expires and the MAH's obligations are assigned to the entity importing the medicine.
f.clause: Article 16. State registration of medicines, part 33
f.processes: Safety governance; Local PV interfaces; Partner & vendor oversight

rows.actor: Holder of the certificate of registration; importer
rows.quote: 33. Where the holder of the certificate of registration of the medicine has notified the Authorised Body, in writing, of the intention to terminate the obligations of the holder of the certificate of registration of the medicine in the Republic of Armenia, the medicine shall still be considered as registered in the Republic of Armenia until the expiry of the term of registration, and the obligations of the holder of the certificate of registration shall be assigned to the entity importing the given medicine as prescribed by the legislation of the Republic of Armenia.
rows.location: Article 16. State registration of medicines, part 33
rows.review_note: Review: kept because the transferred obligations include the Article 17 PV duties. ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Side effect definition: excludes lack of efficacy and overdose
f.statement: A side effect is the emergence of harmful and undesirable phenomena when the product is used in compliance with the instruction for medical use. Absence of efficacy and the consequences of overdose are not considered side effects (lack of efficacy is reported separately under part 10).
f.clause: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 1

rows.quote: 1. Side effect shall be the emergence of harmful and undesirable phenomena in case of use of the product in compliance with the instruction for medical use. The absence of efficacy of the medicine or the consequences of overdose shall not be considered as side effects.
rows.location: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 1
rows.review_note: Review: definition kept because it narrows what is reportable as a side effect (use per label only). ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Operate a GVP-compliant pharmacovigilance system: record side effects, evaluate benefit-risk and notify
f.statement: The MAH is obliged to have a pharmacovigilance system compliant with the Good Pharmacovigilance Practice established by the Authorised Body, to record cases of side effects, to evaluate the risk-benefit ratio and to notify about them as prescribed by the Authorised Body.
f.clause: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 2
f.processes: Safety governance; Case processing & follow-up; Benefit–risk review

rows.actor: Holder of the certificate of registration (marketing authorisation holder)
rows.quote: 2. The holder of the certificate of registration of medicine shall be obliged to have a pharmacovigilance system in compliance with “Good Pharmacovigilance Practice” established by the Authorised Body, record the cases of side effects, evaluate the risk-benefit ratio and notify about them as prescribed by the Authorised Body.
rows.location: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 2
rows.review_note: Review: GVP is the EAEU GVP adopted by the Authorised Body (see MoH Order 322-N). ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Designate a QPPV and, if the QPPV is abroad, a local PV responsible person in Armenia
f.statement: The MAH shall designate a qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance and, where that qualified person acts outside Armenia, shall designate a person responsible for pharmacovigilance in Armenia. The requirements for both are set by the Authorised Body.
f.clause: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 2

rows.actor: Holder of the certificate of registration (marketing authorisation holder)
rows.quote: Holder of certificate of registration shall designate a qualified person to be responsible for pharmacovigilance, and in case the qualified person is acting outside the territory of the Republic of Armenia, shall designate a person to be responsible for pharmacovigilance within the territory of the Republic of Armenia. The requirements for qualified persons and responsible persons shall be established by the Authorised Body.
rows.location: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 2
rows.review_note: Review: split from the PV-system duty (different actor duty). ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Do not publish side-effect information without prior notice to the Authorised Body
f.statement: The MAH may not provide the public with information it has collected on side effects of the registered product without prior notice to the Authorised Body.
f.clause: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 3

rows.actor: Holder of the certificate of registration (marketing authorisation holder)
rows.quote: 3. The holder of the certificate of registration may not provide the public with the information collected with regard to the side effect of the registered product without prior notice to the Authorised Body.
rows.location: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 3
rows.review_note: Review: prohibition recorded as Mandatory. ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Entities in the circulation of medicines must report suspected side effects
f.statement: Healthcare specialists and entities engaged in the circulation of medicines (which includes MAHs, manufacturers, importers and distributors) shall inform the Authorised Body of suspected side effects as prescribed by the Authorised Body.
f.clause: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 4

rows.actor: Healthcare specialists; entities engaged in the circulation of medicines
rows.quote: 4. The healthcare specialists, entities engaged in the circulation of medicines shall inform the Authorised Body of the suspicious side effects as prescribed by the Authorised Body.
rows.location: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 4
rows.review_note: Review: "entities engaged in circulation" per Art. 3(20) covers companies across the supply chain. ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Report extremely harmful (serious) side effects to the Authorised Body
f.statement: The MAH shall inform the Authorised Body, as prescribed by the Authorised Body, of cases of extremely harmful side effects (death, life-threatening, requiring hospitalisation, resulting in incapacity for work, physical mutation or inborn defect). Where an unfavourable risk-benefit ratio is confirmed for such side effects, circulation of the medicine is terminated and it is withdrawn under Article 23(2).
f.clause: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 8
f.processes: Submission operations; Case processing & follow-up; Benefit–risk review

rows.actor: Holder of the certificate of registration (marketing authorisation holder)
rows.deadline: As prescribed by the Authorised Body
rows.quote: 8. The holder of the certificate of registration shall inform the Authorised Body of the cases of extremely harmful side effects (death, posing risk to life, requiring hospitalisation, resulting in incapacity for work, physical mutation or inborn defect) as prescribed by the Authorised Body. In case of extremely harmful side effects (death, posing risk to life, requiring hospitalisation, resulting in incapacity for work, physical mutation or inborn defect) the circulation of the medicine shall be terminated and it shall be withdrawn from circulation as prescribed by part 2 of Article 23 of this Law, where unfavourable risk-benefit ratio has been confirmed.
rows.location: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 8
rows.review_note: Review: time limits delegated to the Authorised Body (EAEU GVP); no deadline_rule. ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Report suspected lack of efficacy, misuse and falsification
f.statement: Healthcare specialists, entities engaged in the circulation of medicines, consumers and the MAH shall also notify the Authorised Body, as prescribed by it, of suspected lack of efficacy, misuse or falsification of a medicine.
f.clause: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 10

rows.actor: Holder of the certificate of registration; healthcare specialists; entities engaged in circulation; consumers
rows.quote: 10. The healthcare specialists, entities engaged in the circulation of medicines, consumers, holder of the certificate of registration shall also notify the Authorised Body, as prescribed by the Authorised Body, of the suspicion of lack of efficacy, misuse, falsification of medicine.
rows.location: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 10
rows.review_note: Review: no change. ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Provide post-registration safety study data when the Authorised Body demands it
f.statement: To evaluate the risk-benefit ratio continuously, the Authorised Body may demand from the MAH data on post-registration safety studies of the medicine performed as prescribed by the Authorised Body.
f.clause: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 11

rows.actor: Holder of the certificate of registration (marketing authorisation holder)
rows.quote: 11. In order to continuously evaluate the risk-benefit ratio, the Authorised Body may demand the data on the post-registration studies of medicine safety, performed as prescribed by the Authorised Body from the holder of the certificate of registration.
rows.location: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 11
rows.review_note: Review: level follows the authority's "may demand". ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

f.title: Be subject to PV inspections at QPPV, local person and contractor sites and pay their cost
f.statement: Compliance of the MAH's pharmacovigilance system with Good Pharmacovigilance Practice is assessed through professional monitoring (inspection) at the place of business of the qualified person and the responsible person, including the places of activity of contractors. The MAH compensates the expenses of the PV system monitoring under a contract.
f.clause: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 12
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Partner & vendor oversight

rows.actor: Holder of the certificate of registration (marketing authorisation holder)
rows.quote: 12. Assessment of compliance to the Rules of “Good Pharmacovigilance Practice” of the system of pharmacovigilance by the holder of the certificate of registration shall be performed through professional monitoring in the location of business of the qualified person and responsible person (including in the places of activity of those performing works on a contractual basis). The Government of the Republic of Armenia shall establish the procedure for recognising the reports of professional monitoring, as well as the reports of monitoring by the competent bodies of other countries. The expenses for the professional monitoring of the system of pharmacovigilance shall be compensated by the holder of the certificate of registration, based on the contract concluded between the parties as prescribed by law. The expert opinion drawn up based on professional monitoring shall be submitted to the Authorised Body.
rows.location: Article 17. Submitting information on side effects and falsified products, part 12
rows.review_note: Review: no change. ARLIS English translation (published 14.08.2026); the Armenian text governs, so confidence is capped below 90.

dates.title: Armenian Law on Medicines (HO-86-N): enters into force
dates.scope: The Law on Medicines as a whole, including the Article 17 pharmacovigilance duties of registration certificate holders
dates.timing_note: Article 31(1): the Law enters into force six months following its official promulgation; the ARLIS act details give 15.12.2016. Later amendments (HO-153-N of 11 April 2024, edited Articles 14, 16 and 17; HO-462-N of 17 December 2025) carry their own transitional provisions, which this text does not reproduce.
